mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing jurisdiction; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization only where required by the receiving Quebec institution; Canadian-issued documents may be certified by a Quebec notary or commissioner of oaths

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against (i) the PCMLTFA politically exposed persons (PEP) definitions and FINTRAC guidance; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Canada's consolidated autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, R.S.C. 1992, c. 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21; (iv) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, with application of the OFAC 50 percent ownership rule, given Apple IAP and Google Play Billing USD payment rails; and (v) Quebec AMF guidance and any financial-institution-derived screening triggers. Adverse-media screening is required for every natural person at or above the 25 percent ownership threshold, and for each corporate UBO at any level.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online enterprise registration portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) using the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) preliminary name search system; alternative federal route: Corporations Canada online filing centre (https://ised-isde.canada.ca/CorporationsCanada) for CBCA articles
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, C.Q.L.R. c. C-11, a Quebec enterprise name must be filed in French; a French-language corporate name is mandatory, an English version may be registered only together with a French version; recognized trademarks may be used without a French version only if French text is accompanied in marketing. Names must be written in Latin-alphabet characters; accents and French orthographic conventions must follow REQ standards; the name must be distinctive, truthful and not cause confusion with existing names in the NUANS database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (requires federal chartered bank authorization)
Trust / Fiduciaire (requires deposit-taking insurance or trust company authorization)
Assurance / Insurance (requires AMF insurer license or certified financial institution status)
Bourse / Stock Exchange (requires recognized exchange designation)
Avocat / Notaire / Ingenieur / Medecin (reserved to members of Quebec professional orders)
Reine / Queen / Royale / Royal / Imperiale / Imperial (implies Crown or governmental connection)
Ministere / Gouvernement / Conseiller fiscal (implies public authority affiliation)
Canada / Quebec / Montreal in a dominant position (may require consent where it suggests governmental sponsorship)
Cooperative (lawful only for duly registered cooperatives)
Police / Gendarmerie / Douane (reserved to state security agencies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ refusal of a proposed name (non-distinctiveness, confusion with an existing NUANS hit, or use of a prohibited token): (1) the applicant submits a written reconsideration request to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching arguments, trademark registration certificates, common-law goodwill evidence and a revised distinguishing element; (2) if the reconsideration fails, the applicant may file a formal demande de revision with the REQ review service; (3) a further refusal may be contested by judicial review before the competent Quebec court (Cour du Quebec or Cour superieure, as applicable), with a parallel option to file a fresh name reservation; (4) Quebec law does not provide a statutory extension of the 90-day reservation window, so a renewed reservation application must be filed if incorporation is not completed within the reserved period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions. A QBCA corporation must maintain a registered office in Quebec capable of receiving service of process and statutory notices; REQ will accept a serviced-office address or corporate-service-provider address with a physical presence, but will not accept a post-office box or mail-only virtual mailbox as the registered office. For Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant underwriting and business banking, the registered office must be supported by verifiable operational substance (e.g., a Canadian management office, corporate agent, or registered agent service in Montreal); a purely virtual mail-drop arrangement is not advisable for this low-risk digital publisher.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified probability: estimated at no more than 5% per annum of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first three years for a low-risk, digitally remote publisher. Revenu Quebec and the CRA do not systematically conduct unannounced corporate-presence visits for this industry; the probability rises to an estimated 10-20% if a GST/QST audit, a FINTRAC suspicious-transaction filing, or a registered-office complaint triggers a field verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the QBCA; the articles may provide for shares without par value and a corporation may be incorporated without issuing any shares; no escrow account condition applies for standard digital-service corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions of the incorporators for the shares set forth in the articles are hereby accepted and the appropriate share certificates are issued; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be and is hereby fixed at the address stated in the notice of registered office, and that the corporation shall maintain all required public records at such address; RESOLVED, that the following individuals be and are hereby appointed as directors and officers of the corporation: [Name] as President and Director, [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer and Director, and [Name] as Director, each to serve until election of successors; RESOLVED, that the banking resolutions and signing authority established by the board are ratified, and the officers are authorized to execute all documents necessary to activate the web-novel subscription platform.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable – the enterprise is classified as a digital content publisher and web-novel platform under NAICS 511130 (Periodical Publishers) and is not subject to manufacturing or industrial licensing in Quebec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for an online-only subscription platform.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Environmental approval branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a digital service with no physical infrastructure, no wastewater discharge, no emissions point source, and no hazardous waste generation; no environmental impact assessment is mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – the platform does not conduct industrial discharges; if the entity later leases office space, compliance with municipal sewer, HVAC, and e-waste recycling rules remains a general building obligation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and occupancy certification are not prerequisites for the web-novel platform itself; if a physical office is leased, the landlord must provide a compliance certificate respecting the Building Code (Qc) and fire safety; employees are covered under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1) and standard liability insurance, with CNESST registration applicable to any payroll staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) - Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec (www.revenuquebec.ca) - Mon dossier d'entreprise portal, administering Quebec corporation tax, QST, and (for Quebec-established businesses) the federal GST/HST under the CRA-RQ single-administration agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or provincially under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) and obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ). Step 2: Register with the CRA via Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts, notably RC0001 (federal corporate income tax) and RT0001 (GST/HST). Step 3: File the single GST/HST-QST registration (form LM-1) with Revenu Québec, which issues the QST number using the NEQ base and the QST program suffix, eliminating a separate federal GST/HST registration for Quebec-established businesses. Step 4: Maintain separate federal T2 and Quebec CO-17 corporate income tax filings, and reconcile Apple App Store / Google Play merchant-of-record financial reports against the registrant's revenue accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Canada/Quebec business corporation is a resident taxpayer subject to federal Part I and Quebec corporate income tax on worldwide income; there is no pass-through or S-corporation equivalence, and the entity is a per se corporation for US check-the-box purposes (Treas. Reg. 301.7701-2(b)(8)); foreign-source digital revenue is taxable in Canada with foreign tax credit relief and controlled-foreign-affiliate (FAPI) rules applying to downstream affiliates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box or pass-through election exists for business corporations. Available elections affecting this structure: (i) non-calendar fiscal-period election (ITA s. 249.1) subject to CRA concurrence; (ii) GST/HST group registration election (Excise Tax Act s. 273) and the corresponding QST group election for closely related Quebec corporations, permitting consolidated indirect-tax compliance; (iii) associated-corporation small-business-deduction allocation under ITA s. 125(7); (iv) Canada's hybrid-mismatch rules, which disallow deductions on hybrid instrument and entity mismatches without any elective opt-out. A US check-the-box election is legally unavailable because Canada is on the per se corporation list.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT-type system: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975%, yielding a 14.975% combined Quebec rate; digital web-novel subscription supplies are taxable supplies of intangible personal property and services taxed at destination (recipient's place of residence) for both GST and QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - small-supplier threshold for both GST and QST; registration is compulsory within 30 days after taxable supplies (including zero-rated export sales) exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; app-store subscription revenue from Canadian consumers counts toward the threshold, and Apple/Google IAP commission statements must be netted according to the merchant-of-record agreement for threshold computation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based invoice stamping, or continuous transaction controls. Mandatory electronic filing applies where thresholds are met: CRA requires e-filing of GST/HST returns and T2 corporate returns for large filers, and Revenu Québec requires electronic QST filing for registrants above prescribed turnover thresholds. Books, vouchers, and electronic records must be retained for six years (ETA s. 286 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act), and monthly reconciliation of Apple/Google Play financial reports to GST/QST accounts is required for audit readiness.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital web-novel subscriptions supplied to non-resident (non-Canadian) recipients are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V (supply of services and intangible personal property to non-residents) and are correspondingly zero-rated for QST, provided the supply is not in respect of Canadian real or tangible property and the subscriber's habitual residence and device app-store territory are outside Canada. Qualifying zero-rated exporters remain GST/QST registrants and may claim full input tax credits and refunds on Canadian business expenses, making substantiation of non-resident status essential. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, but the 180-day settlement benchmark in this dossier governs the completeness of payment documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Zero-rated supply register with per-transaction non-resident evidence: subscriber contract, billing address, IP geolocation, and device app-store territory (country code)
Apple App Store and Google Play monthly financial reports and payout statements evidencing foreign-territory sales and any app-store-remitted GST/HST/QST
Foreign-currency settlement and remittance records: FX conversion reports, bank deposit advices, and payout receipts from Apple/Google payment rails

Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13A) and transport documents (air waybill or bill of lading) - required only where tangible goods are exported; inapplicable to intangible web-novel subscription exports
Six-year retention of all books, vouchers, and electronic records in Canada as required by ETA s. 286 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess unsubstantiated zero-rated exports as taxable supplies within the four-year normal reassessment window, or indefinitely for misrepresentation or fraud, clawing back unremitted GST/QST plus interest and late-filing and late-remittance penalties (up to 6% of the unpaid net tax plus daily compound interest). Gross-negligence false-statement penalties reach 25% of the tax evaded under ETA s. 285 (50% under ITA s. 163(2), with Quebec equivalents under the Tax Administration Act), and knowing falsification may lead to criminal prosecution. Repeated failures may also trigger denial of input tax credit and refund claims, enhanced audit scrutiny of the app-store revenue reconciliation, and publication of sanctions by Revenu Québec.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acts as monetary authority, currency issuer for the Canadian dollar (CAD), and retail payments supervisor under the Retail Payment Activities Act (SC 2021, c. 23; PSP registration regime effective 16 November 2024). It does not operate a foreign exchange control or licensing regime. FX-related supervision is compartmentalized: OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) prudentially regulates the Schedule I banks; FINTRAC administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), including EFT and large virtual currency transaction reporting; and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) enforces cross-border currency reporting. The federal government's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and Criminal Code sanctions regimes must be screened before every cross-border transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account; there are no capital controls, no surrender requirements, and no profit-remittance licensing. A Quebec commercial corporation (federal or provincial) may receive foreign equity injections, repatriate profits, and distribute dividends without Bank of Canada approval. The only compliance friction is tax-based: (i) Part XIII Income Tax Act withholding at 25% on dividends, royalties, and management fees paid to non-residents (treaty-reduced, e.g., 15% dividends / 10% royalties under the Canada–US treaty, frequently 0% on royalties under other applicable treaties); (ii) the GST/HST (5%) and Quebec QST (9.975%) place-of-supply rules for digital services; (iii) the W-8BEN-E filing requirement with US withholding agents, as Apple/Google pay through US or related entities and may treat app-store proceeds as royalties or business income under IRC 871/881 absent treaty relief. No capital-account permission is required from any Canadian authority for inbound investment or outbound profit remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation timeline for export receipts; the platform may keep earnings in USD in a domestic USD sub-account or offshore account without restriction. The only enforceable constraints are reporting: (i) importing/exporting currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to CBSA under PCMLTFA Regulation 19; (ii) cross-border EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC, with the reporting obligation attaching to the financial intermediary, so the platform should pre-notify its account manager; (iii) any CAD 10,000+ cash or EFT transaction conducted with a foreign-exchange dealer is subject to large transaction and beneficial ownership reporting. Apple/Google monthly settlement wires of CAD-equivalent value above 10,000 will consequently trigger automated FINTRAC reporting by the receiving Canadian bank, which the treasury must reflect in its compliance calendar.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Canada does not recognize the EU EMI passport; foreign digital-bank/EMI rails (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) may be used only as secondary collection/payout channels once the operator verifies that the PSP is registered as an MSB with FINTRAC and, for money transmission, with Quebec's Autorité des marchés financiers under the Money-Services Businesses Act (CQLR c E-12.000001). Since 16 November 2024, retail payment services supplied to Canadians are also subject to Bank of Canada supervision under the RPAA, so foreign PSPs serving Quebec users or the platform's payout flows must hold or be affiliated with a designated PSP registration. Legal constraints: (i) Apple/Google settlement proceeds must never be routed to a foreign EMI as the primary treasury; Canadian tax filings and QST registration require a Canadian bank account; (ii) EMI balances are not CDIC-insured; (iii) the platform must not operate an unlicensed money-transfer business for author payouts, meaning each payment must be supported by a specific underlying content royalty obligation and funds must not be commingled beyond 24 hours without bank consent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, every Quebec Schedule I bank requires an in-branch interview at a Montreal or Quebec City branch for the series of directors, the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and at least one signing officer before the corporate account is activated. Remote video verification is permissible under FINTRAC's dual-process identification method (e.g., credit-file match + certified ID copy), but bank risk appetite is low for non-resident directors. For a federal CBCA corporation, at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians (CBCA s. 105(2)); for a QBCA provincial corporation the residency requirement is stricter. The blueprint therefore advises: (i) appoint or retain a Quebec-resident director (legal counsel or accounting partner) with physical presence; (ii) have all non-resident directors/signatories complete notarized ID verification and appear via a sub-30-minute video call with the account manager; (iii) submit the corporate extract (Registraire des entreprises du Québec) and the federal Corporations Canada certification, both dated within 30 days; (iv) present the board resolution (English/French) authorizing account opening and designating daily transaction limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Canadian shareholder / UBO resident in a high-risk or non-treaty jurisdiction (e.g., HK, UAE, BVI, Cayman) holding >10% of the web-novel platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC-compliant Beneficial Ownership Declaration (statutory form); complete corporate organizational chart; certificate of incumbency and constitutional documents of each intermediate entity (apostilled); source-of-wealth letter and supported source-of-funds evidence (12 months of personal/corporate bank statements, tax assessments); registry extracts (e.g., HK Companies Registry, DMCC license, BVI Registry) with English/French translations; signed undertaking to notify the bank of any UBO change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound Apple IAP / Google Play Billing revenue with mismatched settlement amounts or no verifiable commercial contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program License Agreement plus four quarterly App Store Connect Financial Reports; Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement plus four monthly Google Play payout statements; IRS Form W-8BEN-E (claiming Canada-US tax treaty benefits); merchant-processing statements (Stripe/Adyen if used) reconciled to net revenue; an accountant's agreed-upon-procedures letter reconciling app-store subscriptions, virtual currency (coins/keys), and tip revenue to bank deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: All non-resident directors/signatories lacking a Canadian presence or using private mailbox addresses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports (bilingual notary); notarized proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement dated <90 days); banker's reference from their home-country bank addressed to the Canadian account manager; video-KYC dual-process completion per FINTRAC guidance; appointment of a Quebec resident director (for QBCA) or Canadian resident director (for CBCA) with a current REQ extract proving the appointment; a signing authority matrix with limitation amounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model flagged due to in-app tipping / donation mechanics resembling unlicensed money services or gambling
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple App Review approval letter and App Store category certificate; Terms of Use and End-User Licence Agreement defining virtual coins as non-redeemable content-access tokens with zero cash-out value; platform content moderation and age-gate policy; a legal opinion (Quebec counsel) that the subscription/tipping model is not a lottery or wagering transaction under Criminal Code Part VII; an MSB regression checklist demonstrating that the platform never transmits funds on behalf of third parties outside the server-payment framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if federally incorporated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation; a one-year extension may be requested in limited circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A corporation that defaults on its annual return for one year may be administratively dissolved by the Director after prior notice. Restoration requires a court order or Director’s consent, payment of arrears, and compliance with all corporate filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise’s registration in the Quebec register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual declaration is not filed for two consecutive years, the Registrar may strike the enterprise from the register or dissolve the corporation. Revival requires a formal application, payment of prescribed fees and penalties, and confirmation of current directors and information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of each taxation year and its related financial statements must be available; e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, with an additional 10% penalty for repeated failure; statutory interest accrues on unpaid amounts, and the CRA may make arbitrary assessments and register tax arrears as liens.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the corporation’s taxation year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Québec may impose penalties and interest under the Tax Administration Act, assess the corporation by default, and initiate compulsory collection measures after a notice of assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative revenue or asset threshold triggers a mandatory audit for a non-distributing private corporation in Quebec. An independent audit is compulsory only if the corporation is a reporting issuer, a financial institution under Canadian/Quebec legislation, or if shareholders holding a sufficient interest validly require an audit despite the waiver. Non-distributing private corporations may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder agreement or resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may choose IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Corporate income tax returns use the Income Tax Act tax basis with reconciliation from book income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec and CBCA private corporations must maintain an accurate register of individuals with significant control (ISC register). Material changes, including share transfers resulting in 25% or more control, must be recorded in the ISC register within 15 days of the change and made available to enforcement authorities on request. There is no annual public UBO declaration in Quebec; the annual declaration to REQ confirms updated directors, officers and registered office data, which is used by the registrar to maintain ownership transparency files.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Securities Register and share transfer records

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate tax rate (federal rate 15% + Quebec general rate 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No jurisdiction-specific tax holiday for digital web fiction or serialized subscription platforms. A qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may claim the Small Business Deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income, reducing the combined effective rate on that income. Eligible Canadian software-development expenditures may further generate refundable/non-refundable Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits at the federal and Quebec levels.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) using EFILE, approved third-party XML, or through the CRA My Business Account portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; each fiscal period is generally 12 months, including a short fiscal year in the year of incorporation, change of year-end, or discontinuation of business.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year. The balance of federal corporate income tax payable is due no later than two months after the fiscal year-end, or three months for a qualifying CCPC meeting prescribed ownership and taxable-inc ome conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, CRA business number (BN), assigned corporation access number, fiscal year-end, province or territory of jurisdiction, and registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the country of incorporation, country of residence for tax purposes, and the Canadian business number. A non-resident corporation must declare whether it carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada and attach the required information return codes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all commercial activities, including web-novel subscriptions, in-app purchases through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, advertising, digital asset micro-transactions, and licensing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must report only Canadian-source income attributable to its Canadian permanent establishment, notwithstanding the gross revenue recorded in its home-country financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss before income taxes after cost of sales, author royalties, platform hosting, editorial expenses, software amortization, marketing, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses shall be allocated on a reasonable basis to the Canadian permanent establishment and supported by contemporaneous documentary evidence; head-office management fees must satisfy arm's-length standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments reconciling accounting net income to taxable income, including non-taxable dividends, capital cost allowance, reserves, and non-capital loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must file T2 Schedule B and apply the special rules for computing taxes payable in Canada, including the Part I.3 tax interaction and treaty re-sourcing, where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate income tax before and after credits, including the general rate reduction, small business deduction, foreign tax credits, and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are generally ineligible for the small business deduction and must reconcile Part I tax payable using the federal treaty provisions and any Part XIII obligations on outbound distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the T2 triggers a federal penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax, plus 1% per complete month, up to 12 months; a second or repeated failure may attract a 10% penalty plus 2% per month. A grossly negligent false return may be charged a 50% civil misrepresentation penalty, plus accrued interest under the Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically with Revenu Québec through the Services en ligne des entreprises portal or approved professional tax-filing software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the CO-17 covers the same fiscal period as the federal T2 return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The CO-17 return must be filed no later than six months after the fiscal year-end. The balance of Quebec corporate income tax is payable within two months after the fiscal year-end, or three months for qualified SME taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, Quebec Enterprise Registrar (NEQ) number, business establishment address, fiscal year-end, and business activity code corresponding to digital publishing and online subscription services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with a permanent establishment in Quebec must provide its foreign corporate identifier and complete the Quebec establishment registration before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Quebec-source revenue, including subscription fees, in-app content purchases, royalties derived from Quebec readers, advertising revenue, and ancillary digital services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only revenue attributable to Quebec activities or Quebec subscribers shall be reported; inter-provincial allocation follows the place-of-use and permanent-establishment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Deduction section – Cost of sales and expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly incurred to generate revenue, such as platform hosting, author advances and royalties, payment-processor commissions, employee costs, and IT infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must substantiate Quebec expenses separately and cannot deduct charges from non-resident affiliates unless supported by transfer-pricing documentation and fair allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after loss carryovers, reserve claims, amortization, and small-business-deduction eligibility.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation is generally entitled to Quebec loss carryovers only to the extent the losses are connected to the Quebec permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec tax before credits, less refundable and non-refundable credits, including the Quebec SR&ED credit and any applicable multimedia or digital-content tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only Quebec credits for which the business qualifies under the Tax Administration Act; a non-resident paying tax on a Quebec PE may be required to file prescribed schedules and supporting certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid amount plus 1% per month up to 12 months, interest on assessed balances, and a gross-negligence penalty of up to 50% of the understated amount where false statements are made knowingly or with willful blindness.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% of the gross amount paid to a non-resident of Canada under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, subject to reduction or elimination under an applicable Canada tax treaty or the Canada-Quebec provincial interjurisdictional arrangements where domestic rules apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and submit Form NR301 Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty to the Canadian payer before payment, together with a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the residence jurisdiction. The payer must retain the form as support for applying a lower Part XIII rate. If the full 25% has already been withheld, the non-resident must file Form NR7 Application by a Non-Resident of Canada for a Refund of Part XIII Tax Withheld, accompanied by the TRC and relevant trust/ownership documentation, within the statutory reassessment period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding rates are 25% for copyright and IP royalties, and 25% for interest, except where the treaty rate or domestic arm's-length interest exemption applies. Under typical comprehensive Canadian DTAs, royalties are often reduced to 10% (15% for some treaty partners), and interest is reduced to 10% or 0% depending on beneficial ownership and enterprise character. The Canada-US treaty generally provides a 15% dividend rate (5% for 10%-owned subsidiaries), 10% interest, and 10-15% royalties; the payer must apply the principal-purposes test and limitation-of-benefits provision.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is triggered for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate annual value; a Local File is expected where related-party transactions are material to the Canadian entity. A Country-by-Country Report and Master File obligation applies to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not operate an offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the CRA and Revenu Québec apply substance-over-form, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act, and transfer-pricing adjustment rules under section 247. A Quebec web-fiction corporation must demonstrate real office premises, operational decisions, employees, servers, content management, and economic risk in Canada. A conduit or brass-plate corporation that merely invoices subscription revenue from Quebec while bearing no substance is vulnerable to recharacterization, treaty denial, permanent-establishment assertion, and related withholding assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission, concealment, or falsification of web-novel subscription revenue received through Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, direct credit-card rails, or advertising networks; inflating author royalties or fake licence expenses; destroying records; or filing returns without reporting Quebec-source digital income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under section 163(2) of the Income Tax Act of 50% of the amount of tax that would have been understated, plus interest. Criminal conviction under section 239(1) carries a fine equal to 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, imprisonment for up to two years, restitution orders, and publication in CRA tax-evasion conviction bulletins. Revenu Québec imposes equivalent penalties under the Tax Administration Act and may suspend or revoke registrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who participate in or authorize the false reporting may be charged jointly under criminal law, liable for restitution, and personally subject to imprisonment. In criminal proceedings, bail conditions may include surrender of passports and travel bans; CRA and Revenu Québec may also seek civil enforcement against director assets where corporate formalities are used as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Non-Resident Part XIII Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or management charges to non-resident shareholders, authors, or related platform operators without withholding the statutory 25% Part XIII tax, failing to obtain Form NR301 and a certificate of tax residence, or structuring payments as fees to avoid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is liable for the full amount of tax that should have been withheld under section 215 of the Income Tax Act, plus arrears interest and penalties. A gross-negligence penalty of 50% may be added if the omission is intentional. Revenu Québec may reassess the same amount where the payment was deducted in computing Quebec taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted Part XIII tax under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act. CRA may issue a director's liability assessment and commence civil recovery against personal bank accounts and property; wilful evasion in respect of withholding gives rise to criminal liability, including fines, imprisonment, and departure restrictions pending prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring related-party transactions with non-resident web-fiction affiliates, IP-holding companies, marketing intermediaries, or payment-service shell entities at non-arm's-length prices; shifting Canadian reader-revenue profits to a zero-percent jurisdiction through unchecked royalties, content licences, or intra-group mobile-app store charges; failing to file T106 information returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may re-determine taxable income to arm's-length amounts under section 247(2), deny the deduction for excessive payments, apply the transfer-pricing penalty under section 247(3) equal to 10% of the net adjustment where reasonable efforts are not demonstrated, and impose gross-negligence penalties, arrears interest, and treaty-claim disallowance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer-pricing documentation, pressure finance staff to fabricate comparability benchmarks, or direct payment flows to shell entities may be assessed as abettors, made parties to criminal fraud, or held liable for unpaid withholding taxes arising out of the recharacterization. Criminal Code fraud convictions for dishonest earnings through artificial pricing carry imprisonment up to 14 years and court-ordered restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Corporation, Sham, and Economic-Substance Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Quebec-registered corporate vehicle with no office, employees, bank account, board meetings, or operational control while invoicing subscription revenue and funneling profits to foreign tax havens; using nominee directors; failing to maintain financial, contractual, and beneficial-ownership records; or claiming treaty benefits on passive conduit flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA and Revenu Québec may apply the GAAR under section 245 to disallow the tax benefit and reallocate income to the real economic owner. The courts may treat the arrangement as a sham and deem a permanent establishment where substance is absent, resulting in full federal and Quebec tax reassessment, Part XIII withholding on distributions, interest, and up to 50% gross-negligence penalties. Anti-money-laundering authorities may also report the corporate vehicle to FINTRAC and impose monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will carefully pierce the corporate veil when a company is used for fraudulent or dishonest purposes. Directors and beneficial owners may be held personally liable for restitution, including disgorgement of profits, court-ordered compensation to the tax authorities, and, in aggravated fraud cases, imprisonment. Travel restrictions may be imposed by the court at the bail stage, and CRA may obtain third-party garnishment and asset-freeze orders against director assets.
